tasks.title: Galilean moons
tasks.statement: Computer simulation of the planet Jupiter and its 4 Galilean moons is shown on the screen similar to the view you may see through a small telescope. After observing the movement of the moons, please identify the names of the moons that appear at the end of the simulation. (Simulation will be played on screen during the first fifteen minutes and the last fifteen minutes of the exam)

tasks.title: The Moon’s age
tasks.statement: The 60th anniversary celebrations of King Bhumibol Adulyadej's accession to the throne of Thailand (GMT +07) were held on the 8th to the 13th June, 2006. Photographs of the Moon taken at the same hour each night are shown in the task. Assuming that Albert Einstein’s birth was at noon on 14th March, 1879, use the data provided above to find the Moon’s age (number of days after the new moon) on his birth date in Germany (GMT +01). Please show the method used for the calculation in detail. Estimate the errors in your calculation.

parts.question: Find the Moon’s age on Albert Einstein’s birth date with uncertainty and show the calculation method.
parts.reference: Answer: From the figures of the Moon’s phase depicted above, we can conclude that the full moon occurs on June 11th (+/- 0.5 day), 2006. We are going to use this full moon as the reference for calculating the Moon’s age on Albert Einstein’s birthday (March 14, 1879). The student must find out that the approximate time span between June 11th, 2006 and March 14, 1879 is 127 years. There are 31 leap years between the two years. Total days = 46,475 days starting from June 11, 2006 to March 14, 1879. Number of days / synodic month = 46,475 / 29.5306 = 1573.791254. Remainder converted to days from full moon: 6.1644 days from the bottom of the cycle or 20.9297 days into the synodic month. Finally, the Moon’s age on Albert Einstein’s birthday (March 14, 1879) is 20.9 +/- 0.5 days. Marking Scheme: The student must not use the difference between the time zone of Thailand and Germany to calculate the Moon’s age: 0.5 point (wrong answer = 0 point). The student can point out that the June 11, 2006 is a full moon day: 1 point (wrong answer = 0 point). The student can point out that there is an uncertainty in the full moon day = 0.5 day: 1 point (an answer without any uncertainty = 0 point, uncertainty > 0.5 and <= 1 day gets 0.5 points, uncertainty > 1 day gets 0 point). The student gives the correct answer: 5.5 points (if the answer is wrong, look at the detail in the process of calculation. Missing one point of the concept used in the correct calculation = missing 0.5 points until the point is over). An extra 0.2 point for additional considerations.

tasks.title: Solar System objects
tasks.statement: A set of data containing the apparent positions of 4 Solar System objects over a period of 1 calendar year is given in Table 1. Location of observer: Latitude N 18° 47’ 00.0”, Longitude E 98° 59’ 00.0”. Show your method of data analysis carefully and answer the following questions.

parts.question: Put the letters A, B, C and D beside the appropriate objects on the answer sheet (Identify objects A, B, C, and D by names).
parts.reference: Object A: Sun (0.50 points), Object B: Jupiter (0.50 points), Object C: Venus (0.50 points), Object D: Mars (0.50 points).

parts.question: During the period of observation, which object could be observed for the longest duration at night time?
What was the date corresponding to the situation in 3.2?

Assuming the orbits are coplanar and circular, indicate the positions of the four objects and the Earth on the date in 3.3, in the orbit diagram provided. Specify other objects including the Earth together with the correct values of elongation on that date.
parts.reference: Correct position of the Earth relative to the Sun (46º before RA=0h): 1 point. Correct position of object in the orbit: Venus (C) = 0.5 points, Mars (D) = 0.5 points, Jupiter (B) = 0.5 points. Correct value of elongation angle: Venus (C) = 48.07º (0.5 points), Mars (D) = 69.39º (0.5 points), Jupiter (B) = 181.20º (0.5 points).
